summary: A 1941 steel Aermotor tower and log cabin on Strawberry Butte in the Elkhorns; the tower is closed to visitors while the cabin is rented year-round.

facts.design: 65-foot steel Aermotor tower with a 7x7 metal cab, above a one-story log cabin on the ground
facts.status_note: Standing, but no longer an active lookout

access.note: The tower is not open to the public. The cabin is rented to the public year-round, listed on Recreation.gov.

visit.trail_note: Last mile of access is non-motorized only, 10/15 to 5/15 (Forest Service).

facts.agency: U.S. Forest Service, Helena-Lewis and Clark National Forest

events.note: Erected in 1941 as a 65-foot steel Aermotor tower with a metal cab, with a one-story log cabin below

resolved_conflicts.explanation: Firelookout.com calls the cabin a wintertime rental. The Forest Service page and an undated Flickr post say it is rented year-round. The story follows the two year-round sources and reports the disagreement.
NHLR gives 4,989 ft (1,521 m) for the site, which matches the brief's elevation. The Forest Service gives 6,100 feet for the top of Strawberry Butte. The story uses the summit figure.

notes_for_editor: Built year (1941) and the 2005 registration are solid across NHLR, the Forest Service and firelookout.com. Staffing history, notable fires and the year the tower stopped being used were not found in the sources read; staffing is omitted rather than guessed. The brief's conflict note ('They share a register number') does not match the pages: only NHLR US 631 / MT 39 turned up. The Flickr rate of $50 a night is undated and may be stale. NHLR lists a Luke Channer photo, but no image URL was captured, so no photos are added.
